quest.title: A Decision
quest.description: You make new friends amongst the People of the Springs and leave memories behind. It's good to take a break before embarking on a new journey.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x700, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: Black Stone Under a White Stone

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Are you alright, Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: He was a formidable opponent — exactly what I would expect from the First of the Fatui Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I never imagined someone could match you in combat...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If the Tsaritsa sent him here, why would he bring up what happened "five centuries ago"?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yeah, and how much does he know about Natlan...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Harbingers are all driven by their own personal goals. The only purpose that unites them is collecting the Gnoses.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But I'm sure The Captain has his own reasons for being here as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Whatever his motive, we should shift our focus to the Fatui. If they attack again and we're not prepared, we're done for.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No. We're running out of time.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The wound I inflicted should hold him back and weaken him for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm sure you noticed... The power that came to his rescue just now came from the Masters of the Night-Wind.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: In other words, there are traitors among us.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. This could prove to be a very valuable turn of events.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: When we exchanged final blows, I sensed an unusual presence within him. I'll need to investigate further.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Kinich, go to the Masters of the Night-Wind and look into who could have aided the Captain. Speak to Citlali — she should know.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Of course. I'll head out right now. Do you still intend to...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, but fear not.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Natlan's strength has never rested solely in its Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Together, we foresaw the only path that leads to our nation's future. We must trust in that vision now.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Is everything okay, Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Completely fine. Just lamenting the fact that I never got a picture when I could still turn my hair into flames. Hehe, too late, now.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...I just hope the others have a safe journey.

talks.objective: Take a walk around the People of the Springs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like a whole new Paimon after those two days in the hot springs. The Abyss kinda threw a wrench in our relaxation, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, spending time here really has felt like a vacation!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Koholasaurs are so nice, and so fun to play with. Their bellies are super bouncy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and Atea's snacks were so delicious! She gave Paimon some for the road just this morning, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was she up to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yelling at some kids who got caught throwing stones in the hot springs... So, not much has changed since we first met her.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, you guys! Sleep well last night?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! This area is so nice, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Glad you like it! I was thinking of taking you guys out to do some sea-fishing. Later tonight, we can eat whatever we catch. Fresh fish is absolutely delicious right off the grill!

dialogues.speaker: Tonina
dialogues.text: Hey, Mualani!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah? What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Tonina
dialogues.text: The team sent out to fight in the Night Warden Wars has returned.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: And Kachina? Is she back as well?

dialogues.speaker: Tonina
dialogues.text: Kachina... fell in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Tonina
dialogues.text: But, don't worry! The team was victorious, so the Rite of Resurrection will be held at the Stadium soon.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's a relief. The Abyss is cunning, and it was her first time. Mistakes are bound to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Tonina
dialogues.text: Exactly. She deserves to hold her head up high.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, thanks for letting me know. We'll head out in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Geez, she sounded a little anxious there — had me thinking it was bad news for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani, you said the Abyss was "cunning" just now. But, it seems like the Abyss just wants to destroy everything!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, think about all those monsters that attacked your tribe. If there really was some sort of "cunning" plan, wouldn't it make more sense to send them to attack Kachina and her small team?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ummm, not that Paimon wants them to be in any more danger! It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Haha, relax, I get it. The Abyss is difficult to understand, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: At a glance, it certainly seems like the only goal is total destruction. The Abyss isn't a living entity, after all, so what capacity for logic or planning could it possibly possess?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But, through our long history of fighting the Abyss, we've realized things aren't quite so simple.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, the Abyss invaded Teyvat. You know about that, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: During the age of Khaenri'ah?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right. Khaenri'ah suffered greatly during that time, but so did every other nation in Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: And Natlan was the worst affected of all. It took the combined efforts of the then-Pyro Archon and heroes from every tribe to finally repel the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Even so, the effects of the invasion lingered for hundreds of years, only able to be reversed little by little.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Our tribe's waters were contaminated. The Children of Echoes' territory was overrun by dangerous sludge surging from underground. Unrelenting black winds tore across the lands of the Flower-Feather Clan...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It was like each disaster was "designed" for a specific tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the Abyss understood the foundation of each tribe?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Exactly. We once thought that the Abyss' desire for destruction was a sort of primal instinct, but its methods are, in truth, marked by intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We now believe the Abyss has invaded the Night Kingdom, and has the capacity to read the memories of this land at any given moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that's how it became so dangerous and cunning, almost like it knows you inside and out...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yes, and that's why we've been unable to fully eradicate it, even after all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Luckily, the problems left behind by the Abyss have been successfully addressed by the various Pyro Archons we've had over the years.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Now, every tribe is prospering, and things are looking up. I mean, just look at what we managed to do a few days ago! We totally fought them off!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (In other nations, I've seen how much effort it takes to truly eradicate the Abyss.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The people of Natlan live in its shadow every day. Who knows how long it will take for this war to end...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must have had to sacrifice a lot to get to this point...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Every battle, every sacrifice is in pursuit of a future where we get to stop fighting.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Responsibility, duty, unavoidable burden... Everyone in Natlan views the war differently.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But, I believe we WILL be rid of the Abyss one day, and the efforts of all who fought against them will become a story for the ages!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: To think that my name could survive in ballads passed down to future generations... It's kind of romantic.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Everyone has something that drives them forward, you know?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: We have to — not only for ourselves, but for our future.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, let's head to the Stadium. Our fishing trip can wait until Kachina's back with us.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The sea's not going anywhere!

choices.text: You make me want to contribute.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Haha, be my guest! Heroes are always welcome in Natlan.

talks.objective: Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame
Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this place is packed already.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Of course! No one's gonna miss out on the chance to welcome our heroes back from battle, hehe. It's their moment of glory!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina's gonna be so flustered. She's never had this many eyes on her before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, she doesn't seem like the kind of person who likes being the center of attention.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Looks like I'm just in time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich, you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah, a commission ran longer than expected, but I made it. I heard about the incident with your tribe, Mualani. Is everyone alright?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Yeah, it's all taken care of. Our new friend here's got some tricks up {M#his}{F#her} sleeve, by the way. {M#He}{F#She}'s just as strong as Kachina made {M#him}{F#her} out to be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, look! Is it about to start?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That's right. Someone will come out and recite a eulogy, and then we'll sing the Ode of Resurrection together.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: C'mon, let's find a spot with a good view. When the singing starts, just follow my lead, and you'll be fine.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Let's go somewhere higher up, so Kachina can spot us.

response.speaker: Ntotila
response.text: Warriors of Natlan — heed the call of life.

response.speaker: Ntotila
response.text: We are the inheritors of memory and legend.

response.speaker: Ntotila
response.text: Those who grew alongside sun and wind.

response.speaker: Ntotila
response.text: Those who forged our own destiny and future.

response.speaker: Ntotila
response.text: That is Natlan's fire, the lifeblood of our nation.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I could not find Kachina within the Night Kingdom, or locate her Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh. What does that even mean?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Usually, once the Ode is complete, the Pyro Archon and resurrected person will emerge from the flames, but something went wrong...

response.speaker: Lakamha
response.text: What's going on?

response.speaker: Mazatan
response.text: This has never happened before.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Well, I think it's pretty obvious. Clearly, the team sent to fight the Abyss didn't win after all.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Think about it! The Ode rekindles all victors — we've witnessed it countless times.

response.speaker: Tamuin
response.text: Since the Archon couldn't find Kachina in the Night Kingdom, that must mean there's more to this "victory" than meets the eye.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You just haven't gotten over the fact that Kachina beat you in the Pilgrimage!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Pathetic, the both of you...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Your wild guesses are misplaced. We completed our mission.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Maybe YOU did, but who's to say whether that little girl even contributed at all? Maybe she got scared and ran off...

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Why would the Wayob recognize someone like her, even if she was on the winning team.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: How dare you insult a hero of Natlan like that!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Kachina sacrificed herself to repel the Abyss. She doesn't deserve to be subjected to your vile rumors when she's not even here to defend herself!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Calm down, Mualani, there's no point in arguing with the likes of them.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I can't just sit here and let them slander her like that!

response.speaker: Tamuin
response.text: To "insult a hero of Natlan," the person actually has to be a hero.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: You... You!

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Think about it, everyone! Who do you think is really at fault here? A girl who never should've even gone to war...

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Or the great Pyro Archon? Why would the rules of our nation suddenly stop working!?

response.speaker: Lakamha
response.text: That's true. If she wasn't revived, it must mean she failed to achieve victory.

response.speaker: Mazatan
response.text: Maybe the Wayob interpret "victory" in different ways?

response.speaker: Ecate
response.text: I mean, that girl didn't look all that strong to me...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Pyro Archon seems to be deep in thought. Why isn't she putting a stop to the commotion?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kachina wouldn't have run. That's not like her at all!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: No. She's been waiting for this moment for too long!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: No matter how daunting the situation, no matter how scared she might feel, she's always the first person to stand up and face it head-on!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: We don't even know what happened, so don't you dare try to use this as an excuse to vent your anger or slander her reputation.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: Fine. We'll find out what happened soon enough. Then, we'll see who truly deserves glory...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's enough.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: There is no doubt about today's victory, or Kachina's part in it. She is a hero worthy of our admiration and celebration.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: However, the failure of today's ceremony is undeniable. Kachina has not been rekindled, and I offer you all my deepest apologies as I continue to investigate this matter.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: To prevent further casualties, I have decided to suspend the Pilgrimage until this matter is resolved.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: No one is all-knowing. No one is infallible — not even myself.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, doubt is a means by which we seek the truth, not a weapon we wield against others.

response.speaker: Tepexpan
response.text: I—I—I... I didn't mean it that way, Archon, I just...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If there are things you wish to clarify, then ask me directly. Doubt my answer if you wish, but now's your chance. You have concerns? State them.

response.speaker: Tamuin
response.text: N—No, of c—course not...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Even though I have said nothing to change your mind? Then, it would seem the truth never mattered to you at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That guy doesn't even have the courage to answer the Pyro Archon's question. So much for all that glory talk earlier.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I have a question, Archon.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: My friend, Kachina... Do you have any idea where she is? It's extremely important to me!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I know you said you were investigating the situation, but... I'm sorry, that's not enough!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I've already shared everything I know. If you want to learn the truth and rescue your friend sooner, you should join the investigation.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: So, what do you say?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Of course I'll join!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In that case, come see me in the Speaker's Chamber.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: We should join them.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #Oh, and, if it's not too much trouble, could you drop by as well, {NICKNAME}? I'd like to have a chat.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Rest assured, everyone, I'll keep the tribal chiefs informed on the progress of the investigation.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Once again, I apologize for the outcome of this ceremony. If there are no further questions, let's part for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, did she just... ask us to come along?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I believe she did. Let's go. I'd like to know what's going on myself.

choices.text: If only I'd been a bit more perceptive.

talks.objective: Go to the Speaker's Chamber to speak to Mavuika

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we can find Kachina's Ancient Name, I can use the link between them to pinpoint her position within the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Then comes the hard part — You need to visit the Night Kingdom in person and rescue her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, isn't the Night Kingdom a land of souls? Can we even go there?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Under normal circumstances, only the consciousness can enter, but there is a way to go there in person.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: However, know that the Night Kingdom will attempt to repel you, and the Abyss certainly won't leave you be...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's fine by me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Same here. Fighting the Abyss is nothing new for me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It won't be a problem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, uh, Paimon's the only one who's scared? W—Well, if you're going, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's going too.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Citlali of the Masters of the Night-Wind once created an artifact that can be used to communicate with the Wayob. We call it the Spiritspeaker Stone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It was originally used as a ceremonial artifact wielded by the tribal chiefs, but that spiritual quality also means it can be used to search for an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That was the artifact I delivered to the Scions of the Canopy a few days ago. Didn't think I'd be hearing about it again so soon.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for your help, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Your thanks are unnecessary. I will offer you whatever aid I can, but your fellowship and courage are what will truly decide the success of this operation.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Besides, you're the ones helping me. I can only focus on one thing at a time, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I certainly didn't expect our first conversation to be so serious.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've heard all about your accomplishments. Ever since you arrived, I've been hoping to meet you and offer you Natlan's highest level of hospitality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Why?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Why"? Is that not what happened in the other nations you've visited?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, things were pretty complicated at the start... and, y'know, in the middle... But, our reputation's solid nowadays!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, that's more like it. After all, I've heard you're someone who transcends fate.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know quite a lot about me.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Perhaps even more than you can imagine. But we can talk about that some other time.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ideally, this would be the perfect night for a drink and some musical ambiance. But, there are important things to be done.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, I almost forgot... Atea was wounded in the fight against the Abyss. She wanted us to give this to you.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It "embodies fond memories and my strength of will" — that's what she asked us to tell you. She said you'd know what that means...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I didn't think this day would come so soon. The flames of her life force... I can feel them flowing within the talisman.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If things were different, the two of us could have enjoyed the hot springs together while she gave this to me in person. We're supposed to be "hot spring buddies," after all.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, don't worry. This talisman means a great deal to me. I'll take good care of it, and once this is all over, I'll pay Atea a visit.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You said you didn't want to jeopardize the production of Contending Fire... But, that's not at all why you decided to suspend the Pilgrimage, is it...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You're right. Even now, the production of Contending Fire is far from sufficient.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The gradual corrosion caused by the Abyss has resulted in a massive shortage of Pyro energy, and we're currently at the breaking point.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: As things stand, the Pilgrimage is a lost cause. Suspending it allows us to save our strength to defend the tribes.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Abyss has brought catastrophe to Natlan, and Kachina's disappearance in the Night Kingdom is a direct consequence of that.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: *sigh* We can't let the general public know that.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: No. If the public learned that Natlan's destruction was close at hand, there would be immense panic.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, if I said nothing at all, they would have continued to question the integrity of Natlan's heroes.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Another simple choice. The latter was clearly the better solution, but you chose otherwise.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I have never subscribed to the belief that the "right" choice is the one with the fewest "sacrifices."

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Let's go. There's still a way for the Sacred Flame to last a little longer.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: You mean...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes. Come with me.

choices.text: But, looks like we're really making a name for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Sacred Flame must never go out. Not only does it strike fear in the Abyss, but it's also the pillar of Natlan's stability.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, until our heroes are ready, I will sacrifice my power to keep it burning.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But, that can only last so long. I think we should focus on the remaining Ancient Name bearers.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Don't let desperation cloud your judgment...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Those chosen by the Wayob have already embarked on their destined path. It is for them to decide how that journey ends, not us.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: All we can do is support them.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Even so, for you to make this sacrifice... It's not right...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hah, if not me, then who? No other is capable of sustaining the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I possess great strength, but I'm not above my people. This is part of my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's happening at the Stadium!? Did something explode!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It feels like the Archon unleashed her power. She must be fighting a formidable opponent...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we go back and check what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kachina doesn't have that much time.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Have faith in the Archon. She wouldn't lose in a one-on-one confrontation.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Once we find Kachina's Ancient Name, we'll head right back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Let's just keep climbing. Paimon really hopes nothing goes wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The situation is urgent, so I'll get straight to the point. Kachina is undoubtedly a hero of Natlan, and I'm deeply sorry this happened to her.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There's been unrest in the Night Kingdom, but I don't know what's causing it. As a result, I've been unable to track down her location.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Until we find and address the cause of the unrest, the Ode of Resurrection will continue to be ineffective.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that means... Kachina won't be able to come back?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's correct. Not until the problem with the Night Kingdom is resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: How long will that take?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's hard to say.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: ...Kachina always dreamed of fighting the Abyss, of doing her part to defend Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: She wasn't afraid of death because she knew, if it came down to it, the Pyro Archon would be there to bring her back to life...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Whenever we sat down together, exhausted from training, she would always hum the Ode of Resurrection...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: She was supposed to come back to us. We were supposed to hug her and celebrate with her and share her joy...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We supported her every step of the way, but what are we supposed to do now?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Sit peacefully and wait for her to return? Lose ourselves in grief over her death? Tell me — are we her friends? Or her murderers?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's not fair, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's alright. I understand your rage and your grief. Kachina's life means a great deal to me, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Believe me, I want to bring her back as soon as possible. I would give you that peace of mind if I could.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But please hear what I have to say, so I can at least give you a broader picture of the issue we are now facing.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Considering the recent attack on your tribe, I believe the Abyss has found a new means of undermining the rules of our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Sacred Flame — the foundation of our resistance against the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we continue to hold the Pilgrimage and send teams to fight the Abyss, there will likely be more casualties.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, if we stop altogether, the Sacred Flame will only grow weaker. The Abyss will scale up their attacks, and the tragedy we saw with the People of the Springs will only be the first of many.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If we compare the two choices, the former seems to be the lesser of two evils.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...Sorry. I know that may sound harsh, but I bear the Name "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo." Weighing the costs is my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The raw truth can be cruel. But we need to understand it if we want to approach this rationally.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, what would you say, Mualani? This is personal for you, and unlike Kinich, I daresay it's not a simple case of weighing up which course of action is less painful, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: No. I can't choose between them, and I don't want to. Saying that one is preferable over the other is disrespectful to the people who suffered...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You're saying it doesn't matter whether I suspend the Pilgrimage... the consequences will be equally painful.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yes... What happened to Kachina breaks my heart, but I couldn't bring myself to sacrifice other people for her sake...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And that is the crux of the problem. It's not simply a matter of choosing the lesser of two evils.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Either way, there will be people who suffer, and the end result will be the same — belief in the Pilgrimage will waver.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Once doubt has crept in, the people will no longer unite in battle against the Abyss. And that is exactly what the Abyss wants.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Their ultimate goal isn't to break the rules that make the Ode of Resurrection work. It's to destroy the people's faith in them.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: To prevent what happened to Kachina from happening to anyone else, we need to suspend the Pilgrimage, so that is my current plan, and in the meantime, I've made efforts to strengthen each tribe's defenses.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Then, we have to find another way of strengthening the Sacred Flame to keep the Abyss at bay. This won't be easy. I'll need time to figure out the best approach.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I understand your anger, Mualani, but I hope that provided some clarity, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon thought things were gonna get heated for a second, but the Pyro Archon took the time to explain everything so patiently...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I owe you an apology, Archon. I let myself get carried away earlier, and I'm sorry. You're right — we need to focus on finding solutions.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: We could always hold the Pilgrimage without sending a team to fight in the Night Warden Wars. That way, we would still be able to fuel the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've considered that, but the two events have nearly always been linked.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Without the chance to fight the Abyss, Pilgrimage rankings lose their prestige, and competitor numbers will drop.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: With fewer participants, the amount of Contending Fire produced will decrease, and the vicious cycle will continue indefinitely.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So essentially, the Abyss has taken Kachina hostage...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happens if you stay in the Night Kingdom for a long period of time?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You've learned about the concept of Ley Lines during your travels, yes? The Night Kingdom is something similar.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Staying there for a short period of time shouldn't have an effect on the person, but with the Abyss in the picture, it's a different story.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Your sense of self will be devoured until, eventually, you become one with the sea of souls.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Imagine pouring a cup of water into a rushing river. You can try to scoop up another cup, but there's no chance it will be the same water you had before.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I won't sugarcoat it — that is the danger Kachina is currently facing.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Just like you said, Archon, both of these problems need to be addressed...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You can focus all your efforts on dealing with the Sacred Flame. I will go search for Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Abyss poses the same threat to you as it does to her. It is very possible you will not return. Knowing that, do you still choose to go?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina's waiting for us to rescue her — that's all that matters.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I failed to protect her during our campaign, but I can make it up to her now. I choose to go as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um, {NICKNAME}? What do you think?

choices.text: This isn't how it should end for her.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Understood. Then, I'll support you in any way I can.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Masters of the Night-Wind have a technique that can extract an Ancient Name from the Ley Lines.

choices.text: I promised she would have the chance to learn from me.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Friend! That we should meet means that fate has surely smiled upon you. Oh, I have an excellent business proposition for you. If I could just have a moment of your time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why do you merchant types always sound so suspicious?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, don't be like that. The integrity of a Liyue merchant is as steadfast as the Geo Archon themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No harm in hearing you out, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: It's simple. Every day you find me some basic items, and trade them in here for a box full of exciting little curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Even the worst boxes have precious metals inside them... in the form of Mora cast at the Golden House, no less.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, but what's in it for you?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, my business model is a little too complex to explain right now. But, if I have your consistent support in this business deal, then perhaps I will consider letting you in on how it works one day. Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So, whaddya think? Interested?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can't hurt to try it out.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ahh, I see you've willingly returned. That must mean you trust me, even if only a little.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard of scams that start like this though. They rope you in with all the benefits in the beginning, so you let your guard down and that's when they get ya!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hahahaha, please! I don't rely on scams to make my Mora. I rely on my keen sense of business trends.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I was once a merchant of curios. Why curios you ask? Well, because logically speaking, the rarer something is, the more expensive it is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well Paimon's super rare — there's only one in all of Teyvat! So, ah, where's the Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ehehehe, something big is about to happen to our world. And what do you think is going to become scarce once that happens?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What was it I was telling you about yesterday? Ahh yes, supply and demand.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You should know, because of Mondstadt's Stormterror attacks, orchard production was affected and stocks are low. As such, we can expect the price of Mondstadt's wines and ciders to go sky-high, all across Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we know a thing or two about the Stormterror issue...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So, let's see how well you can put two and two together. Tell me, why am I swapping out my curios for basic household items?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because... the whole world is about to be destroyed!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hahahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What was I mentioning yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah yes. Okay, so let's say the world really was on the brink of destruction — how would you even know that anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: That is one of a merchant's other talents. Not only must we read the market and act accordingly, so too must we have our connections.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I happen to be in the know about some very top secret intel. Intel which has come from none other than the economic authority that is the Qixing themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So yesterday I was telling you about... ah, that's right. The Qixing's intel.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The Qixing are the seven greatest merchants in Liyue, who govern over everything to do with our economy, so it goes without saying that their intel is very accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So just what is this intel then?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Stormterror has affected Mondstadt's agricultural production, whilst the Fatui have been getting rather imperious in Liyue and Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: According to confidential intel said to have come from Ningguang, Tianquan of the Qixing herself, the Qixing plan to break ties with the Fatui, and simply let Liyue bear the brunt of the economic impact.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: And when that time comes, the Qixing will be sure to make a pretty penny off the inflated price of everyday items.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where would that leave the poor people of Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: No, no, no, this isn't right... The word about the rift between the Qixing and the Fatui should be out by now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you ever stopped to consider that maybe this "secret intel" of yours is being "leaked" to you on purpose?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You mean, this is a ploy by the Qixing to control small and medium business owners?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on our interactions with others, it seems like you're the only one getting duped.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I... I've been scammed... by Ningguang...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not going to ask me to return my stuff now, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Integrity is the cornerstone of being a merchant, so I won't go back on my word but... But... this is terrible...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, don't give up! You've still got a long life to lead!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You're right. My heart wasn't in the right place. How could the Qixing ever turn their backs on the people of Liyue in order to make a profit? Those everyday items are a necessity for the people to just get by. No one should attempt to corner the market like that, and I shouldn't have allowed myself to go along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Friend, you have seen with your own eyes my very rise and fall. Let my mistakes be a lesson for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That lesson being... to not become a merchant?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm going to need some time to myself to think about what's happened. Business will at least continue to go on, but in the immediate sense that doesn't help me a whole lot...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ah, hello. Do you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here to do some business.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The items needed today are as such.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>I'm here for my Box o' Marvels...</color>

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Here you are: genuine goods at a pleasing price. Worst-case scenario, it'll top up your coin pouch.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here to do some business.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I thought you'd already taken a Box o' Marvels for today? That said, feel free to inspect the others. You'll see I don't cheat any of my customers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you run me through your background again?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm Liben, and once upon a time I sold curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: But I've finally said goodbye to that now that I've made it enough to rub shoulders with the Qixing. No more Mr. Small-Time Merchant for me!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: And that's why you and I are about to start doing business together, and both of us are going to make a handsome sum!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What kind of business?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Simple. You find me a few basic every items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels, full of all kinds of nice little treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you earn any money like this?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: See, this is where the clever bit comes in.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I have recently become privy to some highly confidential intel from the Qixing. It's tough times ahead for the whole of Teyvat, apparently.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: If I start stockpiling everyday essentials now, before long I'll be able to sell them off at much higher prices and make a huge profit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here for my Box o' Marvels...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Here you are: genuine goods at a pleasing price. Worst-case scenario, it'll top up your coin pouch.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: The tale continues on

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Glory passed through generations

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Courage ignites the sky and earth

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Once more, victory heralds Natlan's path

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: We'll wait for you, we'll sing for you

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Come back, brothers, come back, heroes

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Once again, once again, burn bright!
